title: Rosetta App Shortcuts
description: Atomic, contributor-declared capabilities for an app. One file per app at registry/apps/{app_id}/shortcuts.json. Multiple shortcuts may match the same intent; the agent picks by metadata + live stats. Runtime stats (use_count, success_count, success_rate, reliability_score, last_validated) are NOT in this schema — they live in the Postgres ShortcutStats table and are merged in by registry.lookup. NOTE: the action sub-schemas in $defs (keyAction, keyComboAction, typeTextAction, clickAction, menuAction, openAppAction) are duplicated verbatim between workflow.schema.json and shortcut.schema.json. Any change to action types must touch both files. The validate-registry script lints that these $defs are byte-identical.

id.description: Stable kebab-case ID. Unique within this app's shortcuts.json.

intent.description: Plain-language statement of what the shortcut does. Used for fuzzy intent matching by registry.lookup.

parameters.description: Typed inputs the caller supplies at execution time. Substituted into action templates AND verification placeholders. May be empty.

app_versions.description: Free-form version range strings (e.g. "1.85+", "24-27"). Resolution is done by the backend; the schema doesn't constrain syntax in v0.

method.description: How the shortcut accomplishes the intent. Lets ranking favor classes (e.g. search-first over raw key combos).

risk.description: Parking-lot item 3: optional risk classification. Use seed skill pauses for confirmation on non-safe values.

locale.description: Parking-lot item 11: optional BCP-47-style locale (e.g. "en", "en-US", "fr-FR", "ja"). Defaults to the meta.json locale if absent. Use this when authoring a locale-specific variant of an existing shortcut (different menu path, different keyboard shortcut). Matching at lookup time is exact-string in v0; hierarchical fallback (fr-CA → fr → en) is parking-lot 11 work.

produces.description: Parking-lot item 4 (PARTIALLY ACTIVATED 2026-05-03). Optional. Declares that this shortcut emits a named value downstream shortcuts may consume via parameter.consumes. Schema-only in v0; runtime resolution is the chat LLM's responsibility. Type-checking and harness-side validation stay parked.

type.description: Free-text type tag, e.g. "selection", "file_path", "region", "layer_id". Not enumerated; conventions emerge from contributor practice.

key.description: snake_case identifier referenced by consumes.key on a downstream shortcut's parameter.

name.description: snake_case. Substituted into action templates as {name}.

description.description: Human-facing parameter documentation. Surfaces in the generated apps/{app_id}/skill.md and helps the chat LLM choose values.

minimum.description: Numeric lower bound (inclusive). Only meaningful for type:"number". Caller-side constraint; the registry does not enforce at submission time in v0.

maximum.description: Numeric upper bound (inclusive). Only meaningful for type:"number". Caller-side constraint; the registry does not enforce at submission time in v0.

consumes.description: Parking-lot item 4 (PARTIALLY ACTIVATED 2026-05-03). Optional. Declares that this parameter's value should come from a previously-executed shortcut's `produces` output. Schema-only in v0; the chat LLM is the interpreter. Runtime resolution of from_id and type-checking against the producer's `produces.type` stay parked.

from_id.description: Shortcut id whose `produces` block emits the value. Must reference a shortcut in the same app (cross-app composition is parked).

key.description: Must match the `key` declared on the producing shortcut's `produces` block.

metadata.description: Immutable, contributor-declared. Runtime fields (use_count, success_count, success_rate, reliability_score, last_validated) live in Postgres and MUST NOT appear here.

contributor_id.description: GitHub username, or the literal string "seed" for hand-curated v0 entries.

payment_destination.description: Reserved (parking-lot item 15). Always null in v0; populated when the payment economy ships. Field exists from day one — no backfill.

token_cost_estimate.description: Approximate input+output tokens consumed when the agent runs this shortcut. Hand-estimated; refined by usage data later.

speed_estimate_ms.description: Approximate wall-clock milliseconds from action start to verification pass.

submitted_at.description: Author-declared YYYY-MM-DD. Distinct from the actual merge timestamp (which is in the Postgres Submission audit row).

keys.description: Either a single string (platform-resolved by the MCP) or a per-platform map.

text.description: May contain {parameter_name} placeholders that the MCP substitutes at execution time.

platform_specific.description: Workflow.open[] form: signals the MCP to use the app's detection block to launch.

focusWindowAction.description: Parking-lot 9: target a specific window of the frontmost app before sending keystrokes. Resolves the window via osascript (System Events) and brings it to front. If no window matches, the action throws so the agent can recover (try a different match, or fall back to the focused window).

match.description: How to identify the target window. "title_contains" / "title_equals" inspect the window title (case-sensitive); "index" picks the Nth window of the frontmost app (0-based).

value.description: Match value. String for title-based matches (may contain {parameter} placeholders); number for index. Required for all match modes.

app_id.description: Optional. If set, ensure this app is frontmost first; otherwise focus_window targets whichever app is currently frontmost.

rule.description: Named rule the verify() implementation knows how to evaluate against the AX tree (e.g. "active_editor_filename_contains").

value.description: Argument for the rule. May contain {parameter_name} placeholders.

screenshotDiff.description: Compare a pre-action screenshot (passed via observation.before) against a post-action capture. Default behavior (neither bound set) verifies nothing changed beyond max_pixel_diff_ratio (0.02). Setting min_pixel_diff_ratio inverts the assertion to 'verify at least N of pixels changed' — useful for toggles that produce a visible effect AX can't catch. Both bounds may coexist (e.g. min=0.05, max=0.30 for 'something visible changed but not the whole frame').

max_pixel_diff_ratio.description: Pass requires ratio ≤ this value. Default 0.02 unless min_pixel_diff_ratio is set, in which case max defaults to 1 (no upper bound).

min_pixel_diff_ratio.description: Pass requires ratio ≥ this value. Use to verify a visible toggle happened. Default 0 (no lower bound).

hash.description: Hex sha256 of the file's contents.

valueCompare.description: Compare two values. String values in left and right support {parameter_name} placeholder substitution at execution time, matching the convention in typeText / axTreeAssertion / fileCheck.

question.description: Natural-language question passed to the vision/audio model.

expected.description: Expected answer fragment. Match is case-insensitive substring in v0.

oneOf.description: Rectangle resolved against the frontmost window's top-left at capture time. x and y are offsets from that origin.

region.description: Parking-lot 16(c): optional region for the screenshot the agent judges. Without this, verify(interpret_check) captures the frontmost window (per the os_screenshot frontmost_window shorthand). Use absolute coordinates for fixed-position UI; use relative_to:window for window-anchored regions that should follow the app as it moves.

waitForIdle.description: Universal GUI-app-control primitive (Phase 7a, 2026-05-03). Verifies that the frontmost app has finished a long-running operation by polling for responsiveness. Designed for apps with loading states (Photoshop filters / saves, AutoCAD renders, Excel heavy recalcs, Figma exports). Implementation in mcp/src/verify.ts: polls a lightweight osascript probe every `idle_seconds` (each probe with that interval as its timeout); returns passed:true on the first responsive probe, passed:false with error_class "wait_for_idle_timeout" when total wall-clock exceeds `max_seconds`.

max_seconds.description: Maximum wall-clock seconds to wait for the frontmost app to become responsive. Pick generously: a Photoshop save of a 100MB PSD can take 20+ seconds.

idle_seconds.description: Polling interval in seconds. Also used as the per-probe osascript timeout: a probe that returns within this window means the app is responsive. Defaults to 1.
